items.reason: Camrelizumab is given identically in both arms ("Patients in group A will receive neoadjuvant Camrelizumab ... Patients in group B will receive neoadjuvant Camrelizumab"), and the randomised question is the DC vaccine vs placebo; the vaccine is an excluded type, so no candidate remains.

C3: a drug that every arm receives is soc_backbone even if not GBM standard of care, and "the trial's own investigational question decides which agent is the candidate"; here the comparison is "Camrelizumab plus GSC-DCV" vs "Camrelizumab plus Placebo".

Follows from camrelizumab = soc_backbone and the DC vaccine = excluded_intervention_type. The counter-reading is the title/description framing ("Neoadjuvant PD-1 Antibody Alone or Combined With DC Vaccines"; "study the safety and efficacy of Camrelizumab alone or combined with GSC-DCV"), which presents camrelizumab as investigated too.

Given in every arm at the same dose and schedule ("Camrelizumab IV (3mg/kg, up to 200mg)" before and after surgery in both arms); the record treats neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 as the established platform ("Neoadjuvant therapy with anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibodies were confirmed to be helpful") and adds the vaccine as the question.
C3 applies directly (drug every arm receives); the randomised contrast is vaccine vs placebo.
No eligible candidate, so regimen is not_applicable and no partners are recorded.

regimen is not_applicable whenever has_eligible_candidate is false. If XL instead makes camrelizumab a candidate, regimen becomes combination (the vaccine is another antitumour therapy in the experimental arm).

note: S6 (inclusion) depends on this call. C3 supports camrelizumab = soc_backbone (given equally in both arms; randomised question is the DC vaccine), which excludes the trial. The title 'Neoadjuvant PD-1 Antibody Alone or Combined With DC Vaccines' and 'Camrelizumab alone or combined with GSC-DCV' support coder B's reading (camrelizumab investigational, experimental_monotherapy, regimen combination, trial included). No ruling R1-R8 addresses a non-SOC drug given in all arms of a vaccine trial.
